opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nancy Hunter (employee ID E038) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E038.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nancy Hunter (E038) requested admin to Payroll. As a full-time Engineer, admin is only permitted if her role owns the system (Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist), so her maximum is write. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E038 is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; admin is never allowed. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Nancy Hunter (E038) requested admin access to Payroll, but the employee notes conflict on her employment type: one states full-time Engineer (max write, since Engineers do not own Payroll) and the other states contractor with basic security training (max read; admin never allowed for contractors). Given the conflicting evidence, I apply the more restrictive policy. As a contractor with basic training, her maximum is read, and the requested admin exceeds that maximum. Grant read.
